script: セイバールート三日目-16
title: セイバールート三日目-16

pages.ja:
「あ…………つ」
呆然と目が覚めた。
のど元には吐き気。体はところどころがズキズキと痛んで、心臓が鼓動する度に、刺すような頭痛がする。

「あ…………つ」

のど元には吐き気。体はところどころがズキズキと痛んで、心臓が鼓動する度に、刺すような頭痛がする。
pages.en:
“Ah… ngh.”

I wake in a daze.

Nausea clogs my throat. Aches throb through my body, and every beat of my heart drives a needle of pain through my skull.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ah… guh.”
I wake up.
I feel sick. My whole body is in pain, and I have a sharp headache each time my heart throbs.

pages.ja:
「何が
起きた？」
頭痛が激しくて思い出せない。
長いこと廊下で眠っていたせいか、震えがくるほど体は冷え切っている。
唯一確かな事は、胸の破れた制服と、べったりと廊下に染みついた自分の血だけ。
pages.jaRuby:

起きた？」

pages.en:
“What… happened?”

My head hurts too badly to remember.

Perhaps because I lay in the corridor for so long, my body is cold enough to shiver.

The only things I know for certain are my uniform, torn open at the chest, and my blood caked thickly across the floor.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What… happened?”
I can’t remember because of the sharp headache.
My body is cold, probably from lying on the floor for a long time.
The only certain thing is my ripped uniform, and my own blood on the floor.

pages.ja:
「…………っ」
朦朧とする頭を抱えて立ち上がった。
自分が倒れていた場所は、殺人現場のように酷い有様だ。
pages.jaRuby:
「…………っ」
朦朧とする頭を抱えて立ち上がった。
自分が倒れていた場所は、殺人現場のように酷い有様だ。
pages.en:
“…………”

Clutching my clouded head, I force myself to my feet.

The place where I lay looks like the scene of a murder.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…!”
I get up with a hazy head.
The spot where I was lying looks like a murder scene.

pages.ja:
「……くそ、ほんとに……」
この胸を、貫かれたのか。
pages.jaRuby:
「……くそ、ほんとに……」
この胸を、貫かれたのか。
pages.en:
“…Damn it. So it really…”

—So my chest really was pierced.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Damn, I really…”
…Had my chest pierced?

pages.ja:
「……はぁ……はぁ……ぐ……」
こみ上げてくる物を堪えながら、手近な教室に入る。
おぼつかない足取りのままロッカーを開けて、雑巾とバケツを取り出した。
pages.jaRuby:
「……はぁ……はぁ……ぐ……」

おぼつかない足取りのままロッカーを開けて、雑巾とバケツを取り出した。
pages.en:
“…Hah… hah… ngh…”

Fighting down everything rising in my throat, I stagger into the nearest classroom.

My feet scarcely obey me as I open a locker and take out a rag and bucket.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hah… guh…”
Bearing the pain, I enter the closest classroom.
Moving to the locker with unsteady steps, I take out a mop and a bucket.

pages.ja:
「……あれ……なにしてんだろ、俺……」
まだ頭が混乱してる。
とんでもないモノに出会って、いきなり殺されたっていうのに、なんだってこんな時まで、後片づけをしなくちゃいけないんだ、馬鹿。
pages.jaRuby:
「……あれ……なにしてんだろ、俺……」
まだ頭が混乱してる。
とんでもないモノに出会って、いきなり殺されたっていうのに、なんだってこんな時まで、後片づけをしなくちゃいけないんだ、馬鹿。
pages.en:
“…What… am I doing…?”

My head is still in chaos.

I encountered something monstrous and was suddenly killed. What kind of idiot worries about cleaning up at a time like this?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Huh… what am I doing…?”
I’m still confused.
Why do I still
think I
have to clean up, when I’ve just met something totally outrageous and been killed instantly? Am I an idiot?

pages.ja:
「……はぁ……はぁ……くそ、落ちない……」
……雑巾で床を拭く。
手足に力が入らないまま、なんとかこびりついた血を拭き取って、床に落ちていたゴミを拾い集めてポケットに入れた。
……証拠隠滅、というヤツかもしれない。
朦朧とした頭だからこそ、そんなバカな事をしたのだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
「……はぁ……はぁ……くそ、落ちない……」
……雑巾で床を拭く。
手足に力が入らないまま、なんとかこびりついた血を拭き取って、床に落ちていたゴミを拾い集めてポケットに入れた。

pages.en:
“…Hah… hah… Damn it, it won't come out…”

…I scrub the floor with the rag.

There is no strength in my arms or legs, but somehow I wipe away the blood caked there, gather the bits of rubbish scattered over the floor, and stuff them into my pocket.

…Destroying the evidence, I suppose.

Perhaps only a mind this dazed could make me do anything so absurd.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Haa… haa… damn, it won’t come off…”
…I wipe the floor with the mop.
With unsteady hands, I manage to get the blood wiped off, and pick up any trash lying around and put it into my pocket.
…Maybe I’m destroying the evidence.
I’m still in a daze, so perhaps that’s why I’m doing something so absurd.

pages.ja:
「……あ……はぁ……はぁ……はぁ……」
雑巾とバケツを片づけて、ゾンビのような足取りで学校を後にした。
……歩く度に体の熱が上がる。
外はこんなにも冷たいのに、自分の体だけ、燃えているようだった。
pages.jaRuby:
「……あ……はぁ……はぁ……はぁ……」
雑巾とバケツを片づけて、ゾンビのような足取りで学校を後にした。
……歩く度に体の熱が上がる。
外はこんなにも冷たいのに、自分の体だけ、燃えているようだった。
pages.en:
“…Ah… hah… hah… hah…”

I put away the rag and bucket, then leave the school with the gait of a corpse.

…Every step sends my temperature higher.

The air outside is bitterly cold, yet my body alone feels as though it is burning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Ah… haa… haa… haa…”
I put back the mop and bucket, and leave the school like a zombie.
…I get hotter as I walk.
The air is so cold, but it feels like my body is burning.

pages.ja:
……家に帰る頃には、とうに日付が変わっていた。
屋敷には誰もいない。
桜はもとより、藤ねえもとっくに帰った後だ。
pages.jaRuby:

桜はもとより、藤ねえもとっくに帰った後だ。
pages.en:
…By the time I make it home, midnight has long since passed.

The house is empty.

Sakura is gone, of course, and even Fuji went home hours ago.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…When I get home, the day has already changed.
There’s no one home.
Neither Fuji-nee nor Sakura is around now.

pages.ja:
「……あ……はあ、はあ、は
あ」
どすん、と床に腰を下ろした。
そのまま床に寝転がって、ようやく気持ちが落ち着いてくれた。
「……………………」
深く息を吸い込む。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Ah… hah, hah, ha—ah.”

I drop heavily onto the floor.

Once I lie flat, my mind finally begins to settle.

“……………………”

I draw a deep breath.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Ah… haa, haa, haa.”
I collapse to the floor.
I lie on the ground and finally calm down.
“……”
I take a deep breath.

pages.ja:
大きく胸を膨らますと、罅が入るかのように心臓が痛んだ。
……いや、それは逆だ。
実際ひび割れていたどころじゃない。
穴の開いていた心臓が塞がれて、治ったばかりだから、膨張させると傷が開きかけるのだ。

pages.en:
As my chest expands, pain cracks through my heart.

…No. That is backward.

It was far worse than cracked.

The hole in my heart has only just closed and healed. Expanding my chest nearly pulls the wound open again.
pages.mirrorMoon:
When I inhale, my heart cries in pain as if cracking apart.
…No, that’s wrong.
It wasn’t just cracked.
It had a hole in it, but it healed, and the wound tries to open up again when I inhale.

pages.ja:
「……殺されかけたのは本当か」
それも違う。
殺されかけたのではなく、殺された。
それがこうして生きているのは、誰かが助けてくれたからだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……殺されかけたのは本当か」
それも違う。
殺されかけたのではなく、殺された。
それがこうして生きているのは、誰かが助けてくれたからだ。
pages.en:
“…So I really was almost killed.”

No. That is wrong too.

I was not almost killed. I *was* killed.

I am alive now because somebody saved me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…So it’s true that I was almost killed.”
No, that’s wrong too.
I wasn’t almost killed… I was actually killed.
But I’m still alive in spite of that, because someone saved me.

pages.ja:
「……誰だったんだ、アレ。礼ぐらい言わせてほしいもんだけど」
あの場に居合わせた、という事はアイツらの関係者かもしれない。
それでも助けてくれた事に変わりはない。いつか、ちゃんと礼を言わなくては。
pages.jaRuby:
「……誰だったんだ、アレ。礼ぐらい言わせてほしいもんだけど」

それでも助けてくれた事に変わりはない。いつか、ちゃんと礼を言わなくては。
pages.en:
“…Who was it? I'd at least like the chance to thank them.”

Whoever it was happened to be there, which might make them an associate of those men.

Even so, they saved me. That does not change.

Someday, I have to thank them properly.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I wonder who it was. I should at least thank them.”
Since the person was there, that person might have something to do with them.
But that makes no difference to the fact that the person saved me. I have to thank them one of these days.

pages.ja:
「あ……ぐ……！」
気を抜いた途端、痛みが戻ってきた。
同時にせり上がってくる嘔吐感。
「あ……は、ぐっ……！」
体を起こして、なんとか吐き気を堪える。
「っ……ふ、っ……」
制服の破れた箇所、むき出しになっている胸に手を触れた。
助けられたとはいえ、胸に穴が開いたのだ。
あの感覚。
あんな、包丁みたいな槍の穂先がずっぷりと胸に刺さった不快感は、ちょっとやそっとじゃ忘れられない。
「……くそ。しばらく夢に見るぞ、これ」
目を瞑れば、まだ胸に槍が刺さっている気がする。
そんな錯覚を振り払って、ともかく冷静になろうと努めた。
「……よし。落ち着いてきた」
毎晩の鍛錬の賜物。
深呼吸を数回するだけで思考はクリアになり、体の熱も嘔吐感も下がっていく。

pages.en:
“Ah… gh…!”

The moment my concentration lapses, the pain returns.

Nausea surges up with it.

“Ah… hah… ngh…!”

I sit up and somehow force it back down.

“Ngh… h—”

I touch my bare chest through the hole torn in my uniform.

Saved or not, I had a hole driven through me.

That sensation.

The nauseating feel of a spearhead like the blade of a kitchen knife sinking deep into my chest is not something I will forget easily.

“…Damn it. I'm going to be dreaming about this for a while.”

When I close my eyes, I can still feel the spear buried in me.

I push the illusion away and concentrate on calming down.

“…All right. That's better.”

Perhaps my nightly training deserves the credit.

After only a few deep breaths, my thoughts clear, the heat in my body subsides, and the nausea begins to ebb.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ah… guh…!”
The moment I let my guard down, the pain returns.
At the same time, I feel like vomiting.
“Ah… hah, guh…!”
I sit up and resist the sickness.
“…Huh…”
I place my hand on my bare chest where the uniform is ripped.
Even though I was saved, I did have a hole in my chest.
That feeling.
Such an unpleasant feeling, a spearhead entering my body, isn’t something I can forget easily.
“…Damn, I’ll have nightmares about this for a while.”
If I close my eyes, it feels like the lance is still in me.
I shake off that illusion and try to calm down.
“…All right, I’m starting to calm down.”
The result of all that training every night.
Just taking a few deep breaths clears my mind, and the heat and nausea vanish from my body.

pages.ja:
「それで、アレの事だけど」
青い男と赤い男。
見た目は人間だったが、アレは人ではないと思う。
pages.jaRuby:
「それで、アレの事だけど」
青い男と赤い男。

pages.en:
“Now, about those things…”

The man in blue and the man in red.

They looked human, but I do not believe either one was.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So, about those guys…”
A man in blue and a man in red.
They looked human, but I don’t think they were.

pages.ja:
幽霊の類だろうか。
だが実体を持ち、生きている人間に直接干渉できる幽霊なんて聞いたことがない。
しかもアレは喋っていた。自分の意志もあるって事は、ますます幽霊とは思いにくい。
……それに肉を持つ霊は精霊の類だけと聞くが、精霊っていうのは人の形をしていないんじゃなかったっけ……？

pages.en:
Were they some kind of ghost?

But I have never heard of ghosts with physical bodies, capable of interfering directly with the living.

They could speak, too. The fact that they possessed wills of their own makes it even harder to think of them as ghosts.

…Besides, I was taught that the only spirits with flesh are elementals. Aren't elementals supposed to be inhuman in form…?
pages.mirrorMoon:
Were they like ghosts or something?
But I’ve never heard of ghosts with form, able to associate directly with people.
And they were talking too. If they have their own will, it’s hard for me to think of them as ghosts.
…I’ve heard that the only ghosts with a body are spirits, but aren’t they shaped differently from humans…?

pages.ja:
「……いや。問題はそんなじゃなくて」
他に、もっと根本的な問題がある筈だ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……いや。問題はそんなじゃなくて」
他に、もっと根本的な問題がある筈だ。
pages.en:
“…No. That isn't the real problem.”

There must be something else. Something more fundamental.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…No, that’s not the problem.”
There’s another fundamental problem.

pages.ja:
……殺し合いをしていた二人。
……近所の家に押し入ったという強盗殺人。
……何かと不吉な事件が続く冬木の町。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…Two men fighting to the death.

…The robbery and murder at a nearby house.

…One ominous incident after another in Fuyuki.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Those two who were killing each other.
…The murderous burglar that has appeared in the neighborhood.
…The ongoing ominous events in Fuyuki City.

pages.ja:
「………………」
それだけ考えて、判ったのは自分の手には負えない、という事だけだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………」
それだけ考えて、判ったのは自分の手には負えない、という事だけだ。
pages.en:
“………………”

Thinking it over teaches me only one thing: this is beyond me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
All I can tell with such thoughts is that it’s way out of my league.

pages.ja:
「……こんな時、親父が生きてれば」
胸の傷があまりに生々しかったからか、口にするべきじゃない弱音を吐いていた。
pages.jaRuby:
「……こんな時、親父が生きてれば」
胸の傷があまりに生々しかったからか、口にするべきじゃない弱音を吐いていた。
pages.en:
“…If only Dad were still alive at a time like this.”

Perhaps the wound in my chest is still too vivid. A weakness I should never speak aloud escapes my lips.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…If Father was still alive…”
Perhaps because the wound on my chest is so vivid, I complain about things I shouldn’t.

pages.en:
“—Idiot. You already decided that even when you don't understand, you'll do whatever you can.”

I can complain afterward.

First I have to choose—whether to involve myself or stay away—

“—!?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Idiot. I’ve already decided to do whatever I can, even when I don’t understand.”
Complaining comes later.
First, I have to decide whether or not it’s my concern.
“…!?”

pages.ja:
屋敷の天井につけられていた鐘が鳴る。
ここは腐っても魔術師の家だ。
敷地に見知らぬ人間が入ってくれば警鐘が鳴る、ぐらいの結界は張ってある。

pages.en:
The bell fixed to the ceiling of the house begins to ring.

Whatever its shortcomings, this is still a mage's home.

At the very least, a bounded field has been laid over the grounds—enough to sound an alarm whenever a stranger enters.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The bell hung from the ceiling rings.
This is a magus’s house, even if only a poor one.
There is a boundary field that alerts me when a stranger enters the property.

pages.ja:
「こんな時に泥棒か
」
呟いて、自らの愚かさに舌を打つ。
そんな筈はない。
pages.jaRuby:
「こんな時に泥棒か

そんな筈はない。
pages.en:
“A burglar, now of all times—”

I mutter the words, then click my tongue at my own stupidity.

Of course it is not.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“A burglar, at a time like this…?”
As I speak, I realize my foolishness.
That can’t be it.

pages.ja:
このタイミング、あの異常な出来事の後で、そんな筈はない。
侵入者は確かにいる。
それは泥棒なんかじゃなく、物ではなく命を奪りにきた暗殺者だ。
だって、あの男は言っていたじゃないか。
『見られたからには殺すだけだ』、と。

pages.en:
Not now. Not after everything abnormal that happened tonight.

There is unquestionably an intruder.

But they have not come to steal my possessions. This is an assassin here to take my life.

After all, that man said it himself.

*Now that you've seen us, all that remains is to kill you.*
pages.mirrorMoon:
With this timing, right after that strange incident, that can’t be it.
There’s an intruder.
Not a burglar, but an assassin who’s here for my life.
Because I remember that guy saying…
‘You saw us, so die.’

pages.ja:

」

物音一つしない闇の中、確かに
あの校庭で感じた殺気が、少しずつ近づいてくる。

“—”

The house is perfectly still.

In the darkness, without so much as a footstep, the murderous intent I felt in the schoolyard draws steadily closer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”

“Ah—!?”

Pain tears through my right arm.

“…?”

It happens in an instant.

With a casual thrust too swift for me to react, the man drives his spear forward.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ahhh!?”
Pain assails my right arm.
“…?”
It happened in an instant.
The man’s lance is thrust, without time for me to react.

His spear thrusts forward as though the poster does not exist. The paper blade knocks it aside, leaving the point to graze my right arm and nothing more.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I would have faced my second death with that blow.
But what prevented it was my newly-made sword.
He must have thought it was just paper.
The lance, thrust as if the poster wasn’t there, was deflected by it and only skimmed my right arm.

“…Well, now. That's an unusual trick.”

All expression vanishes from the man's face.

Not a trace of his carelessness remains. He watches my every movement with the eyes of a beast.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Wow. That’s a strange technique you’ve got there.”
The man’s expression goes away.
His carelessness disappears, and he’s now staring at me with beast-like eyes.

そいつを前にして少しでも気を緩ませた自分の愚かさを痛感する。

pages.en:
“Ah—”

I made a mistake. Imagining I had a chance was unforgivable arrogance.

—The thing before me is a demon beyond the bounds of reason.

I feel the full weight of my stupidity in letting my guard down before him for even a moment.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Agh.”
I screwed up. I was just being stupidly optimistic when I thought I could do something.
The thing before me is a monster beyond belief.
Painfully, I realize my foolishness for letting my guard down even slightly against him.

pages.ja:
……そう。
本当に死に物狂いだったのなら、頭上からの一撃を奇跡的にやりすごせた後、脇目も振らずに窓へ走っておくべきだったのだ……！

pages.en:
…Of course.

If I were truly fighting for my life, then after miraculously evading the attack from above, I should have run for the window without looking aside…!
pages.mirrorMoon:
…That’s right.
If I’d been really desperate, I should have ran frantically to the window as soon as I miraculously avoided his first attack…!

pages.ja:
「ただの坊主かと思ったが、なるほど……微弱だが魔力を感じる。心臓を穿たれて生きている、ってのはそういう事か」
槍の穂先がこちらに向けられる。

pages.en:
“I took you for an ordinary boy, but I see… Faint as it is, I can feel magical energy. That must explain how you survived having your heart pierced.”

The spearpoint turns toward me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I thought you were just a kid, but I see… I do feel some magical energy from you, even though it’s weak. That must be why you’re alive even after I stabbed you through the heart.”
He points his lance at me.

」
防げない。

pages.en:
“—”

I cannot stop it.

I cannot stop an attack that moves like a flash of light.

If only his weapon were a sword, I could at least brace myself, however fast he might be.

But that is a spear.

A sword traces a line. A spear becomes a point.

How can I defend against a point when I cannot even read the motion that begins it?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
I won’t be able to block it.
I can’t possibly block that lightning-fast blow.
If his weapon were a sword, I might have been able to at least prepare for it.
But that’s a lance.
A sword follows a line, but a lance has a point.
How am I supposed to block a blow from a point that I can’t even see coming?

The man’s body descends.
In that instant…
His lance is swung, sideways.

He allowed me to block twice, then rewarded me with a single chance to strike.

…And I spent that one absolute opportunity on nothing but postponing death.

Therefore—he sees no value in crossing blades with me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The man was just playing with me.
He let me hit him once, since I blocked him twice.
…But I used up my one and only chance for just a makeshift attack.
That’s why he sees no point in fighting me anymore.

The man brings the deflected spear back into position.

In that infinitesimal hitch in his movement—that opening, if it can even be called one—

“tell me what to do, you bastard—!”

Without looking behind me, I leap backward through the window.

“
You’ve let me down. I’ll just kill you now, kid.”
He readies his lance again.
“Say…”
During that small unnecessary movement…
“…What you want, you idiot!”
Without looking behind me, I jump out the
window.
window…!

with no certainty at all, twist my whole body and strike behind myself—!
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Haa, haa, ha…”
I break the window with my back and roll outside.
I roll a few times, get up, and…
“Haa!”
Without a thought, I turn and swing behind me.

My swing knocks aside the spear already thrust toward me. The man hesitates for the barest instant.

—Just as I predicted.

If I leapt through the window, he was certain to pursue.

And he would catch me before I could rise and strike to kill.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hmh…!”
The man hesitates a moment, as I deflected his lance thrust.
As I expected.
If I jumped out the window, he would definitely come after me.
And he would kill me even before I could get up.

That is why I trusted that a fatal thrust would come and swept my sword sideways with every ounce of strength I had.

Too late meant instant death. Too early meant missing and dying in the opening afterward. It was a reckless gamble—but given the gulf between our abilities, there was no danger of *me* being too fast.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s why I expected the fatal blow and swung at it.
It was a bold plan. I would have died if it was a second too late or a second too early. But considering the difference in our skill, I could never have been too early.

The result was perfect. I won my bet and deflected the man’s lance…!
